nodes.content:
# Project rules

Write clear code and keep changes small.

Before finishing a file, re-read the docstring and list every error condition it describes. Add explicit checks that raise the documented exception (for example ValueError) for invalid arguments, such as negative or out-of-range values, and confirm each check runs before any work is done.

Import every module the file uses (for example itertools) at the top of the file, and run through each function once to confirm no name is undefined.
nodes.diff:
diff --git a/AGENTS.md b/AGENTS.md
--- a/AGENTS.md
+++ b/AGENTS.md
@@ -1,3 +1,7 @@
 # Project rules
 
 Write clear code and keep changes small.
+
+Before finishing a file, re-read the docstring and list every error condition it describes. Add explicit checks that raise the documented exception (for example ValueError) for invalid arguments, such as negative or out-of-range values, and confirm each check runs before any work is done.
+
+Import every module the file uses (for example itertools) at the top of the file, and run through each function once to confirm no name is undefined.

nodes.hypothesis: The take and distribute failures came from skipping error cases the docstring names, so a habit of checking the docstring sentence by sentence before answering should catch those omissions. It is a general self-review step rather than a rule about any one task.

nodes.hypothesis: Missing imports cause NameErrors, and a rule that only says "import everything" does not make the agent look for them. A final pass that checks every name used in the file against its definitions and imports should catch these before the answer is given.

Write clear code and keep changes small.

Before answering, scan the whole file from top to bottom. For every module, function, or variable name used, confirm it is imported or defined in the file, and fix any that are not.
